title: Aurora - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the incident from 2027-02-25 where customers experienced elevated latencies and timeouts. We reviewed the timeline, confirmed root cause as a combination of KV cache eviction patterns and an aggressive autoscaling policy, discussed mitigations already rolled out, agreed on a short-term rollback/fallback plan, and defined benchmarks and next steps for reliability improvements and a formal RCA writeup.
topics: Root cause: KV cache eviction + autoscaler decision loop
Mitigations deployed (cache tweak, autoscaler config, fallback model routing)
Security and compliance concerns (audit logs, KMS)
Next steps: benchmarks, pilot, formal RCA
action_items: Devon Patel (Redwood SE) - Provide detailed autoscaler config diff and proposed changes - due 2027-03-04
Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM) - Share incident timeline doc + customer-facing RCA draft - due 2027-03-05
Emily Zhang (Aurora SRE) - Run the suggested benchmark script on staging and share results - due 2027-03-08
Maya Chen (Redwood AE) - Confirm credits/SLAs and send updated commercial note - due 2027-03-03
next_steps: Redwood to send patched autoscaler config and cache TTL recommendations
Customer to run staging benchmark and validate latency percentiles
Schedule 1:1 deep-dive with Aurora SREs for KV cache behavior (week of 2027-03-07)
Finalize and publish RCA to Aurora and internal stakeholders
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-01
Time: 15:30 - 16:25 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Samir Rao (Aurora VP Eng), Emily Zhang (Aurora SRE), Priya Nair (Aurora Security)

00:00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. quick ack, sorry again about the outage last week, we want to run through what happened, what we've done, and sync on next steps. Maya here from redwood.
00:00:18 Samir Rao: thanks, maya. appreciate you following up. we had ~8% timeouts at peak for our patient-text endpoint, roughly 30 minute impact window, customer escalations to product.
00:00:33 Emily Zhang: yeah the 99th went from 280ms to over 1.8s, and we saw retries from our side leading to cascading load.
00:00:45 Devon Patel: quick note - our initial telemetry shows a tight correlation between cache evictions and spike in token compute. there was a sudden pattern of long prefix requests that invalidated the kv cache, and then autoscaler started provisioning pods but the startup latency plus cold kv's caused the tail.
00:01:10 Priya Nair: can you explain "kv" cache? sometimes the terms get fuzzy in our org.
00:01:18 Devon Patel: sure, kv cache is the key-value cache for transformer key-values - basically the model's cached activations for prefixes. when those get evicted frequently, each request requires more compute. we saw large similar prefixes which killed hit rates. apologies, sometimes the transcript may say k v cache or K-V cache.
00:01:42 Samir Rao: we also noticed the autoscaler tripped a few times during the same window; is that a redwood autoscale config or our k8s HPA?
00:01:50 Devon Patel: it's a config in our runtime orchestrator that talks to your cluster; the decision loop was aggressive because the CPU-based signals were noisy during the cache-miss flood. TLDR: the autoscaler overshot then undershot as pods came up slowly.
00:02:10 Lena Ortiz: action items coming out of this call include both short term rollback/fallbacks and medium term changes to cache TTL and autoscaler logic.
00:02:23 Emily Zhang: thanks. can you summarize what you've already patched? what did you push last night?
00:02:30 Devon Patel: yeah we pushed three quick mitigations: 1) increased KV cache TTL for the affected model family, 2) smoothed autoscaler sensitivity (longer evaluation intervals + higher thresholds), and 3) enabled model fallback routing to a slightly smaller quantized variant for tail requests. those were live as of 02:00 UTC.
00:02:56 Samir Rao: did that immediately bring p99 down?
00:03:00 Devon Patel: partially — p99 dropped to ~650ms within 20 minutes and stabilized ~420ms after the fallback routing fully kicked in. there was a residual impact due to queued retries on client side.
00:03:18 Priya Nair: from a security/compliance standpoint we need to see the audit trail for those config changes and confirm KMS usage for keys in the private deployment.
00:03:29 Maya Chen: absolutely, lena will share the change set and the audit logs. for KMS, we're using customer-managed keys where configured; we'll validate that for your tenant.
00:03:40 Priya Nair: ok, please cc our secops.
00:03:44 Lena Ortiz: noted, we'll include secops and your engineering manager on the RCA distribution.
00:03:50 Samir Rao: one question — why did the cache TTL need to be increased? weren't we using adaptive eviction?
00:03:58 Devon Patel: good q. the eviction heuristic is adaptive but it uses LRU with some heuristics tuned to typical prefix distributions. rare large-prefix bursts defeat the heuristics, so the quick fix increased TTL to keep hot prefixes alive longer. medium-term we plan a heuristic improvement that recognizes repeated long-prefix patterns.
00:04:20 Emily Zhang: you mentioned quantized variant fallback, any accuracy regressions we should be worried about?
00:04:27 Devon Patel: we saw negligible quality delta on our eval sets for the affected prompts, but we'll share detailed prompt-set level metrics. for safety we've limited fallback to tail only and kept default path unchanged.
00:04:40 Samir Rao: the business ask from our side — we need guaranteed SLOs for the endpoint and some remediation (credits) for the incident window. can you speak to that?
00:04:51 Maya Chen: yes, we'll include a commercial note on credits in the follow-up email. we can also propose a dedicated capacity pilot if you want predictability; Redwood Dedicated can avoid noisy neighbor and autoscaler churn, though we've seen some customers use dedicated to get better tail SLOs—but i want to be clear about cost tradeoffs.
00:05:12 Samir Rao: cost conversation later, first we need the technical fix.
00:05:18 Emily Zhang: also, can you reproduce locally or should we provide a corpus to reproduce the exact prefix pattern?
00:05:26 Devon Patel: help from your side would speed this. if you can share an anonymized set of request traces (we only need token sequences and timestamps), we can run a targeted benchmark in our staging.
00:05:36 Samir Rao: yes we can do that, we'll scrub PHI and share.
00:05:40 Maya Chen: great, lena will send secure upload instructions (s3 pre-signed or SFTP) with specs.
00:05:48 Priya Nair: for the secure upload, we need end-to-end encryption in transit and rest; do you support customer-managed keys for any storage you stage?
00:05:57 Lena Ortiz: we support customer KMS for private deployments and can use pre-signed S3 to your own bucket if that helps. we'll include options in the instructions.
00:06:10 Devon Patel: one more technical note — the autoscaler evaluation used CPU util as the main signal; that is noisy when many requests hit uncached paths because initial compute spikes then tails off. our proposal is to add token-rate and KV hit-rate as additional signals so decisions are more stable.
00:06:28 Emily Zhang: token-rate signal sounds useful. can you quantify how much it would reduce oscillation?
00:06:34 Devon Patel: early sims show a ~40% reduction in decision flips for similar workloads, but we need production testing.
00:06:44 Samir Rao: timeline wise, what's realistic for the heuristic improvement vs the quick config change?
00:06:50 Devon Patel: config changes are immediate (done), heuristic code change + QA is ~2-3 weeks, plus a Canary rollout. the token-rate addition to autoscaler could be staged in 1-2 weeks for config and metrics, but fully validated in ~3 weeks.
00:07:05 Priya Nair: from compliance — we want to see the audit logs and proof of change within 48 hours.
00:07:11 Maya Chen: we'll do that. lena will deliver logs and a draft RCA in 48 hours.
00:07:16 Lena Ortiz: noted.
00:07:20 Samir Rao: regarding permanence — do you plan to change the default TTLs for the model catalog or only tenant-scoped?
00:07:28 Devon Patel: tenant-scoped by default for now; we don't want global changes without broad validation. if this pattern repeats across multiple tenants we'll propose a catalog change.
00:07:40 Emily Zhang: another ask — we need to measure end-to-end customer impact including retries from our side; we saw retries increase overall RPS during that window. any guidance on client-side backoff recommendations?
00:07:51 Devon Patel: yes we recommend jittered exponential backoff with a max retry count of 2 for low-latency endpoints, and use conditional retry only on gateway 5xx/504. we'll share a snippet in the follow-up.
00:08:04 Samir Rao: ok.
00:08:08 [00:08:08 silence / note: cross-talk and brief AWS notification sound]
00:08:30 Maya Chen: quick commercial note — we recognize the impact and will include a credit proposal; lena, can you handle the wording?
00:08:36 Lena Ortiz: yes, i'll include a few tiers: pro-rata credits for the incident window, plus an optional trial of dedicated capacity with a short-term discount.
00:08:48 Priya Nair: we'll need that in writing.
00:08:51 Maya Chen: absolutely.
00:08:54 Devon Patel: on a related tangent, we saw some mis-labelling in telemetry where model ids got swapped in a small percentage of traces; that complicated triage. we're fixing the labeling in the collector.
00:09:06 Emily Zhang: that would help a lot.
00:09:09 Samir Rao: let's talk about the formal RCA content. what are you planning to include?
00:09:14 Devon Patel: timeline of events, root cause analysis (cache eviction pattern + autoscaler coupling), mitigations applied, long-term fixes, and monitoring/alerting improvements. plus an appendix with relevant logs and config diffs.
00:09:29 Priya Nair: please include exact timestamps and hashes of config files for audit.
00:09:34 Lena Ortiz: will do.
00:09:38 Maya Chen: ok, i want to open to questions from the customer team.
00:09:42 Emily Zhang: can you run the stage benchmark with our anonymized traces and include p50/p95/p99, and the breakout for cache-hit vs cache-miss?
00:09:51 Devon Patel: yes we will.
00:09:54 Samir Rao: any blockers on your side to do these tests in staging?
00:09:58 Devon Patel: no blockers; the main thing is we need sanitized traces and an access window for a canary run.
00:10:05 Priya Nair: security: we'll provide scrubbed traces and an IAM role for temporary access.
00:10:11 Lena Ortiz: great.
00:10:14 Maya Chen: nearing half an hour in script, let's recap the key commitments: 1) Redwood will deliver audit logs + config diffs within 48 hours, 2) SE will provide autoscaler diff + proposed change by 2027-03-04, 3) Customer runs benchmark and shares results by 2027-03-08, 4) Redwood drafts RCA by 2027-03-05.
00:10:36 Samir Rao: sounds good.
00:10:40 Emily Zhang: i also want the option to schedule a deeper SE session to walk through tracing and agent-level internals.
00:10:46 Devon Patel: happy to do a 90-minute deep dive. we can schedule after we see the first benchmark.
00:10:53 Samir Rao: ok schedule it for w/o 2027-03-14 maybe.
00:10:58 Maya Chen: lena will propose slots.
00:11:02 [short pause]
00:11:20 Devon Patel: quick technical addendum — for the medium-term improvement, we may introduce a hybrid cache policy that accounts for both recency and prefix-length similarity; that should make the cache robust to repeated long prefixes.
00:11:36 Emily Zhang: interesting. any estimate on memory overhead?
00:11:40 Devon Patel: small uptick (~5-8%) for the affected model family, we can cap per-tenant memory.
00:11:48 Priya Nair: only if it's tenant-capped.
00:11:51 Devon Patel: agreed.
00:11:54 Samir Rao: last question — do you have a playbook for customers to flip to fallback models automatically if latency breaches a threshold?
00:12:02 Devon Patel: yes, we do have a routing policy that can be threshold-triggered; we tuned it in this incident to route tail requests to quantized variant. we can help you tune thresholds.
00:12:15 Maya Chen: ok let's move to close, we'll confirm all deliverables in the follow-up email. thanks for the time, we'll be in touch.
00:12:24 Samir Rao: thanks, appreciate it.
00:12:28 Emily Zhang: thanks all.

[Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and truncated words, speaker labels may be slightly off due to auto-attribution.]

End of meeting.
